newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends higher despite bearish Iraq news.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends higher despite bearish Iraq news.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended higher Wednesday despite U.N. approval of an oil pricing formula for the Iraq oil-for-food deal which would bring $2 billion of oil to the market.
"It was bearish news, but it was also pretty much expected," said Jim Ritterbusch, a trader with Sweeney Oil, of news of the U.N. approval.
January crude settled 13 cents higher at $23.75 a barrel. December heating oil finished 0.73 cent up a gallon at 71.97 cents while December gasoline ended 0.34 cent up at 69.35 cents a gallon.
Under the oil-for-food deal, the United Nations would ease sanctions against Iraq and allow Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil in exchange for humanitarian aid.

On Monday, the United States was expected to approve the pricing formula for the oil after Iraq agreed to deal's terms. Final approval of the formula was made Wednesday by the U.N. Security Council sanctions committee on Iraq.
Approval of the oil pricing plan, however, is not the final step. Among the remaining tasks are an inspection of oil metering equipment on December 5 by the Dutch firm Saybolt.
Dealers said U.N. approval of the pricing formula was assumed after the United States indicated Monday it would approve the formula.

Crude prices were also supported by several oil ministers of the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) calling for a rollover of the group's production ceiling of 25.03 million barrels a day at the OPEC meeting in Vienna.
Meanwhile, the December contract expiry in refined products Wednesday fueled a late session rally in heating oil prices as traders scrambled to cover short positions.

"Shorts expected refined products to end lower like they have in the last several expiry days. This time they were wrong," said a dealer, explaining traders had to pay a premium to cover short positions on expiry day this time.
NYMEX will be closed Thursday and Friday due to the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
